{{Short description|Research method developed by Richard Solomon}}
The '''Solomon four-group design''' is a [[research method]] developed by [[Richard Solomon (psychologist)|Richard Solomon]] in 1949.<ref>{{cite web | last1 =Navarro | first1 =Mario | last2 =Siegel | first2 =Jason T. | title =Solomon Four-Group Design | quote="The Solomon four-group design, developed by Richard Solomon in 1949, was devised to overcome the problem of pretest sensitization." | url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323412815 | date = 2018 | accessdate = 22 November 2019 | publisher=[[SAGE Publications]]}}</ref> It is sometimes used in [[social science]], [[psychology]] and medicine. It can be used if there are concerns that the treatment might be sensitized by the [[Pre- and post-test probability|pre-test]].<ref>Introduction to Research in Education by Donald Ary, Lucy Jacobs, Christine Sorensen</ref> In addition of the usual two groups (treatment and control), it has a second pair of groups who do not receive a pre-intervention evaluation. 
==Structure==
The structure of the trial is shown in the table :{{cn|date=November 2023}}
{| class="wikitable"
|+ The four groups in the Solomon design
|-
! Group !! Pre-intervention !! Intervention !! Post-intervention
|-
| 1 || Test || Treatment || Test
|-
| 2 || Test || Control || Test
|-
| 3 || No test || Treatment || Test
|-
| 4 || No test || Control || Test
|}

The first two groups receive the evaluation test before and after the study, as in a normal two-group trial. The second groups receive the evaluation only after the study.{{cn|date=November 2023}}

The effectiveness of the treatment can be evaluated by comparisons between groups 1 and 3 and between groups 2 and 4.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}}. In addition, the effect of the pre-treatment evaluation can be calculated by comparing the control group who received the pre-treatment evaluation with those who did not (groups 2 and 4).

Various statistical treatments for the Solomon four-group design have been put forward, including [[Fisher's method#Relation to Stouffer's Z-score method|Stouffer's Z]] and [[Monte Carlo method|Monte Carlo]].<ref>{{cite web | author =Sawilowsky, Shlomo S.; Markman, Barry S. | title =Another Look At The Power Of Meta-Analysis In The Solomon Four-Group Design | version = | publisher =[[Education Resources Information Center]] | quote="This paper demonstrates that a meta-analysis technique applied to the Solomon Four-Group Design (SFGD) can fail to find significance even though an earlier 'weaker' test may have found significance." | date =1988 | url =https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED316556.pdf | accessdate = 22 November 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author =Sawilowsky, Shlomo S.; Kelley, D. Lynn; Blair, R. Clifford; Markman, Barry S. | title =Meta-Analysis and the Solomon Four-Group Design | journal =The Journal of Experimental Education | version = | publisher =[[JSTOR]] | quote="The present study is a Monte Carlo demonstration." | date = 1994 | volume =62 | issue =4 | pages =361–376 | doi =10.1080/00220973.1994.9944140 | jstor =20152427 }}</ref>
